questions.title: Which of the following cytokines is secreted by Th1 cell:
questions.question: Which of the following cytokines is secreted by Th1 cell:

explanations.A: Incorrect. IL-4 is a signature Th2, not Th1, cytokine.
explanations.B: Incorrect. IL-5 is a signature Th2 cytokine, promoting eosinophil activity.
explanations.C: Incorrect. IL-7 supports lymphoid development from stem cells, not a characteristic Th1 secretion.
explanations.D: Incorrect. IL-13 is a Th2 cytokine, functionally related to IL-4.
explanations.E: Correct. IFN-gamma is the defining Th1 cytokine, produced by activated Th1 cells (as well as NK cells and cytotoxic T cells) to activate macrophages and drive cell-mediated immunity against intracellular pathogens. This IFN-gamma output is what distinguishes the Th1 subset functionally from Th2 cells, which instead secrete IL-4, IL-5 and IL-13.

questions.learning_objective: Identify IFN-gamma as a Th1-secreted cytokine.

field_notes.keySource: printed answer table, hegazy.pdf (Q1-7 strip, bottom of p.16)

questions.title: Which of the following cytokines is inhibitory:
questions.question: Which of the following cytokines is inhibitory:

explanations.A: Incorrect. IL-4 is a Th2 cytokine that drives IgE class switching, not an inhibitory cytokine.
explanations.B: Correct. IL-10 is one of the two classic inhibitory (immunosuppressive) cytokines, along with TGF-beta. It dampens macrophage MHC-II expression, IL-12 production and Th1-driven IFN-gamma output, restraining the immune response.
explanations.C: Incorrect. IL-5 promotes eosinophil growth and activation, an effector rather than inhibitory role.
explanations.D: Incorrect. IL-13 functions alongside IL-4 in Th2/allergic-type responses, not as an inhibitory cytokine.
explanations.E: Incorrect. IL-7 supports lymphoid development, not immune inhibition.

questions.learning_objective: Identify IL-10 as an inhibitory cytokine.

field_notes.keySource: printed answer table, hegazy.pdf (Q1-7 strip, bottom of p.16)

questions.title: Which of the following molecules is produced early in the course of viral infection and serves to slow the infection of adjoining cells?
questions.question: Which of the following molecules is produced early in the course of viral infection and serves to slow the infection of adjoining cells?

explanations.A: Incorrect. CRP is an acute-phase protein that enhances phagocytosis and complement activation, not the early antiviral mediator described here.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Mannose-binding lectin is a complement-pathway acute-phase protein, not the early antiviral cytokine described here.
explanations.C: Correct. Type I interferon (interferon-alpha) is produced early in viral infection, chiefly by the infected cell itself and by plasmacytoid dendritic cells, and acts on neighbouring, still-uninfected cells to induce an intracellular antiviral state that slows the infection's spread to adjoining cells. Because this response depends only on the infected cell's own sensing machinery rather than antibody or T-cell help, it is available within hours, well before an adaptive antiviral response could develop.
explanations.D: Incorrect. IgM is the first antibody isotype in a primary humoral response, but it is not the rapid, non-antibody antiviral mediator this question describes.

questions.learning_objective: Identify interferon-alpha as the early antiviral cytokine that slows viral spread to adjoining cells.

questions.title: A 52-year-old woman had malaise, fever and non-productive cough. Her temperature was 38 degrees C. Which of the following cytokines is responsible for the rise in her temperature:
questions.question: A 52-year-old woman had malaise, fever and non-productive cough. Her temperature was 38 degrees C. Which of the following cytokines is responsible for the rise in her temperature:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Neither IL-3 nor IFN-gamma is a classic endogenous pyrogen; they do not directly explain the fever.
explanations.B: Incorrect. TGF-beta is an inhibitory cytokine, not a pyrogen, and IL-2 is not a pyrogen either.
explanations.C: Correct. IL-1 and TNF-alpha are the classic endogenous pyrogens: they act on the hypothalamic thermoregulatory centre to raise the body's set-point temperature, producing the fever seen here as part of the systemic acute-phase response to infection. This same pyrogen pair also drives the other systemic features of the acute-phase response, including malaise and the hepatic proteins that accompany a bacterial or viral infection like this one.
explanations.D: Incorrect. IL-2 is not a pyrogen; while TNF-alpha correctly belongs in the answer, IL-2 does not pair with it here.

questions.learning_objective: Identify IL-1 and TNF-alpha as the endogenous pyrogens responsible for fever.

field_notes.keySource: printed answer table, hegazy.pdf (Q1-7 strip, bottom of p.16)

questions.title: IFN-gamma is produced by:
questions.question: IFN-gamma is produced by:

explanations.A: Incorrect alone. Th1 cells are a genuine IFN-gamma source, but not the only one.
explanations.B: Incorrect alone. NK cells are a genuine IFN-gamma source, but not the only one.
explanations.C: Incorrect alone. Cytotoxic T cells are a genuine IFN-gamma source, but not the only one.
explanations.D: Correct. IFN-gamma is a pleiotropic cytokine produced by several activated lymphocyte populations together: Th1 cells, NK cells and cytotoxic T cells all secrete it as part of the cell-mediated response, converging on the same macrophage-activating and MHC-upregulating effects. Because so many different activated lymphocyte types converge on the same cytokine, IFN-gamma functions as a shared signal that links innate (NK) and adaptive (Th1, Tc) cytotoxic responses together.

questions.learning_objective: Identify Th1, NK and Tc cells as sources of IFN-gamma.

questions.title: All of the following cytokines are produced by macrophages except:
questions.question: All of the following cytokines are produced by macrophages except:

explanations.A: Incorrect (this IS a macrophage product in this framing). IFN-gamma is credited to activated lymphocytes/NK cells rather than macrophages as its primary source, but among these options it is IFN type I that is the clearly non-macrophage answer here.
explanations.B: Incorrect (this IS a macrophage product). IL-12 is a classic activated-macrophage cytokine.
explanations.C: Correct. Type I interferon is produced chiefly by virally infected cells and plasmacytoid dendritic cells, not by macrophages, whose own cytokine repertoire in this course is the IL-1/IL-6/IL-12/IL-18 set. Grouping type I interferon with the macrophage-derived set is therefore a common exam trap, since its actual source is the infected cell and plasmacytoid dendritic cells instead.
explanations.D: Incorrect (this IS a macrophage product). IL-6 is part of the macrophage-derived pro-inflammatory cytokine set.
explanations.E: Incorrect (this IS a macrophage product). IL-18 is part of the macrophage-derived cytokine set alongside IL-12.

questions.learning_objective: Identify type I interferon as not a macrophage-derived cytokine, unlike IL-12, IL-6 and IL-18.

questions.title: IL-10 is characterised by all of the following except:
questions.question: IL-10 is characterised by all of the following except:

options.C: Decrease MHC class II on APCs

explanations.A: Correct — this is the false statement. IL-10 DECREASES, not increases, IFN-gamma production by Th1 cells. Suppressing Th1-driven IFN-gamma output is exactly how IL-10 dampens cell-mediated immunity.
explanations.B: Incorrect (this is true). IL-10 is produced by macrophages, regulatory T cells and Th2 cells.
explanations.C: Incorrect (this is true). IL-10 decreases MHC class II expression on antigen-presenting cells, reducing their ability to present antigen.
explanations.D: Incorrect (this is true). IL-10 decreases IL-12 production by macrophages, further dampening Th1-promoting signals.

questions.learning_objective: Correct the reversed claim that IL-10 increases Th1 IFN-gamma production; IL-10 decreases it.

field_notes.keySource: printed answer table, hegazy.pdf (Q1-7 strip, bottom of p.16)

questions.title: Which is false about TGF-beta:
questions.question: Which is false about TGF-beta:

options.D: Together with IL-1, IL-6, IL-23 promotes Th17 development

explanations.A: Incorrect (this is true). TGF-beta is a signature Treg-secreted cytokine, alongside IL-10.
explanations.B: Correct. This is the false statement. TGF-beta directs antibody class switching to IgA, the mucosal-secretion isotype, not to IgG.
explanations.C: Incorrect (this is true). TGF-beta inhibits macrophage and T-cell activity, consistent with its role as an immunosuppressive cytokine.
explanations.D: Incorrect (this is true). TGF-beta together with IL-1, IL-6 and IL-23 promotes Th17 differentiation.

questions.learning_objective: Correct the misconception that TGF-beta drives class switching to IgG; it drives switching to IgA.

questions.title: Which of the following cytokines isn't induced by superantigen:
questions.question: Which of the following cytokines isn't induced by superantigen:

explanations.A: Incorrect (this IS induced). Superantigen-driven T-cell activation triggers a surge of IL-2.
explanations.B: Incorrect (this IS induced). TNF is among the pro-inflammatory cytokines released in the superantigen-driven cytokine storm.
explanations.C: Incorrect (this IS induced). IFN-gamma is released as part of the massive T-cell activation superantigens cause.
explanations.D: Incorrect (this IS induced). IL-4 can also be released amid the broad, polyclonal T-cell activation superantigens trigger.
explanations.E: Correct. IL-1 is chiefly a macrophage-derived pro-inflammatory cytokine responding to pathogen products directly, rather than a cytokine characteristically induced by superantigen-driven T-cell activation itself. Superantigen activation instead massively boosts T-cell-derived cytokines such as IL-2, TNF, IFN-gamma and IL-4, which is why those four are the ones genuinely induced here.

questions.learning_objective: Identify IL-1 as not characteristically induced by superantigen-driven T-cell activation.

questions.title: Activation of macrophages is best achieved by:
questions.question: Activation of macrophages is best achieved by:

explanations.A: Incorrect. IL-1 is itself a macrophage product (and a pyrogen), not the principal activating signal macrophages receive.
explanations.B: Incorrect. TGF-beta inhibits, rather than activates, macrophages.
explanations.C: Incorrect. IL-2 chiefly drives T-cell proliferation, not macrophage activation.
explanations.D: Correct. IFN-gamma, produced by Th1 cells, NK cells and cytotoxic T cells, is the principal cytokine that activates macrophages, enhancing their ability to kill intracellular pathogens and upregulating their MHC expression. Th1-derived IFN-gamma is therefore the key link between the adaptive T-cell response and the innate macrophage effector arm in clearing intracellular pathogens.
explanations.E: Incorrect. IL-4 is a Th2 cytokine associated with humoral/allergic responses, not macrophage activation.

questions.learning_objective: Identify IFN-gamma as the principal macrophage-activating cytokine.

field_notes.keySource: printed answer table, hegazy.pdf (Q8-15 strip, bottom of p.17)

questions.title: IL-2 is produced mainly by:
questions.question: IL-2 is produced mainly by:

explanations.A: Correct. IL-2 is the principal cytokine driving T-cell proliferation and clonal expansion, and it is produced mainly by activated Th1 cells (CD3+ helper cells secreting it once activated). This IL-2 signal is what drives the clonal expansion of both helper and cytotoxic T-cell populations once they have received antigen and costimulatory signals.
explanations.B: Incorrect. NK cells produce IFN-gamma and mediate cytotoxicity, but are not the main source of IL-2.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Macrophages produce IL-1, IL-6, IL-12 and IL-18, not IL-2.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Th2 cells are characterised by IL-4, IL-5 and IL-13, not IL-2.

questions.learning_objective: Identify Th1 cells as the main source of IL-2.

field_notes.keySource: printed answer table, hegazy.pdf (Q8-15 strip, bottom of p.17)

questions.title: Which of the following increase expression of MHC class II:
questions.question: Which of the following increase expression of MHC class II:

explanations.A: Incorrect. IL-1 is a pro-inflammatory pyrogen, not the cytokine credited with upregulating MHC class II here.
explanations.B: Incorrect. IL-2 drives T-cell proliferation, not MHC class II expression.
explanations.C: Incorrect. IL-12 drives Th1 differentiation, not MHC class II upregulation.
explanations.D: Incorrect. IL-10 DECREASES, not increases, MHC class II expression on APCs — the opposite effect.
explanations.E: Correct. IFN-gamma increases MHC class II expression on antigen-presenting cells, enhancing their ability to present antigen to CD4+ T cells. Upregulated MHC class II in turn amplifies the whole CD4+ T-cell response, since more peptide-MHC-II complexes are available for recognition.

questions.learning_objective: Identify IFN-gamma as the cytokine that increases MHC class II expression.

field_notes.keySource: printed answer table, hegazy.pdf (Q8-15 strip, bottom of p.17)

questions.title: Type I interferon acts by:
questions.question: Type I interferon acts by:

options.A: Increase expression of MHC class II molecule

explanations.A: Incorrect. Increasing MHC class II expression is an IFN-gamma (type II interferon) action, not a type I interferon one.
explanations.B: Incorrect alone. Increasing NK-cell activity is a genuine type I interferon action, but it is not the only one.
explanations.C: Incorrect alone. Inducing an antiviral state in neighbouring cells is a genuine type I interferon action, but it is not the only one.
explanations.D: Correct. Type I interferon acts by both increasing NK-cell activity and inducing an antiviral state in surrounding, still-uninfected cells. It does not increase MHC class II expression, which is instead an IFN-gamma-specific action.

questions.learning_objective: Identify NK-cell activation and antiviral-state induction as type I interferon actions.

field_notes.keySource: printed answer table, hegazy.pdf (Q8-15 strip, bottom of p.17)

questions.title: Development of Th1 is promoted by:
questions.question: Development of Th1 is promoted by:

explanations.A: Correct. IL-12, produced chiefly by activated macrophages and dendritic cells, is the principal cytokine that drives a naive CD4+ T cell to differentiate along the Th1 pathway. Once Th1 cells differentiate under IL-12's influence, they go on to secrete IFN-gamma themselves, reinforcing the same Th1 programme in a positive feedback loop.
explanations.B: Incorrect. IL-4 drives Th2 differentiation, the opposing subset, not Th1.
explanations.C: Incorrect. IL-3 is a haematopoietic growth factor, not a Th1-differentiation signal.
explanations.D: Incorrect. IL-5 is a Th2-associated cytokine promoting eosinophil activity, not a Th1-differentiation signal.

questions.learning_objective: Identify IL-12 as the cytokine that drives Th1 differentiation.

field_notes.keySource: printed answer table, hegazy.pdf (Q8-15 strip, bottom of p.17)

questions.title: An example of an interleukin with anti-inflammatory properties:
questions.question: An example of an interleukin with anti-inflammatory properties:

explanations.A: Incorrect. IL-22 is associated with mucosal/barrier defence and Th17/Th22-type responses, not classed as an anti-inflammatory interleukin here.
explanations.B: Incorrect. IL-1 is a pro-inflammatory pyrogen, the opposite of anti-inflammatory.
explanations.C: Incorrect. IL-17 is the signature pro-inflammatory Th17 cytokine.
explanations.D: Correct. IL-10 is one of the two classic anti-inflammatory (inhibitory) cytokines, alongside TGF-beta, dampening macrophage and Th1 activity to restrain the immune response. Its anti-inflammatory action complements the pro-inflammatory cytokines (such as IL-1 and IL-17) by putting a ceiling on how far the immune response escalates.
explanations.E: Incorrect. IL-2 drives T-cell proliferation, a pro-response rather than anti-inflammatory action.

questions.learning_objective: Identify IL-10 as an example of an anti-inflammatory interleukin.
